title: Factorization of every projective BGG operator on real projective space with the standard round connection into explicit second-order curvature factors followed by its Young projector
author: Michael G. Eastwood; A. Rod Gover
work: The BGG Complex on Projective Space
source_version: Official SIGMA 7 (2011) article 060, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2011.060; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The order and tensor symmetries of a BGG operator come from highest-weight representations and projective connection changes. The authors turn a noncommuting connection-change product into a uniform factorization through a Riccati algebra, prove its realization faithful, and identify arbitrary-order factors by their Chebyshev annihilators. This supplies explicit high-order curved formulas with fixed Young symmetries, beyond a routine differential-operator expansion.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Theorem4 on RP^n,n>=2, with its standard round metric normalized R_ab=(n-1)g_ab, and the BGG complex of a finite-dimensional irreducible SL(n+1,R) representation with dominant integral labels a1,...,an. For its rth operator,0<=r<n,s=a_(r+1)+1, and the prescribed Young projector pi, the operator is pi applied to the product of (nabla squared+j squared g) for j=s-1,s-3,..., ending in nabla if s odd or the j=1 factor if s even, exactly as printed. Source flat-BGG normalization fixes the overall scale.
original_metadata.editorial_warning: The algebra lemma normalizes the curvature scalar to one, while the geometric formula inserts the source round Schouten tensor g. Preserve the original Young diagrams, tensor projections and symmetrized multiplication conventions; no interpretation as an unrestricted scalar differential operator or arbitrary-curvature formula.
